Applying target-encoding principles to SASRec transition features: leave-one-transition-out subtracts the current observed edge a→b from both C(a,b) and its row total, removing direct self-counting. Repeated edges and overlapping windows from the same user can still expose related target information. Leave-one-user-out subtracts that user’s entire contribution; user-level cross-fitting partitions users and builds each fold’s table exclusively from other folds. This prevents the held-out user’s targets entering their transition features. Any learned priors, smoothing parameters or support thresholds must respect the same exclusion. These are adaptations of [cross-fitting guidance](https://sklearn.org/stable/modules/preprocessing.html); [CatBoost’s analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.09516) cautions that leave-one-out alone does not guarantee freedom from target-dependent artifacts.

For each training example, construct one adjusted table and score every candidate j using it: P_adj(j|a)=[C_adj(a,j)+αq_adj(j)]/[Σ_k C_adj(a,k)+α]. Use the identical smoothing, fallback and score transformation for positives and negatives. Under transition exclusion, remove the actual a→b observation once before either lookup; never subtract a hypothetical a→negative edge or use full counts for negatives. Otherwise candidate features depend on their labels, creating an artificial discrimination shortcut. [H2O documents exclusion-based training encodings](https://docs.h2o.ai/h2o/latest-stable/h2o-docs/data-science/algo-params/data_leakage_handling.html).

Full training counts at validation/inference are legitimate when held-out targets never enter the table. However, they change feature support: a singleton edge excluded during training reappears at inference, potentially activating an uncalibrated transition boost. Probabilities need not increase because denominators also change. Smooth toward a training-only prior, regularize the transition weight, and select it using validation with the exact inference table; inspect performance by transition support.
